newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria stamps presence on oil island near Benin.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria stamps presence on oil island near Benin.

text.p: Nigeria has commissioned a water project on Tongeji island near neighbouring Benin where crude oil was recently discovered, the Weekend Times newspaper reported on Saturday.

A lavish ceremony was held on the island on Friday attended by the military administrator of the southwestern Ogun state Wing Commander Sam Ewang and traditional chiefs led by the paramont ruler of Tongeji Chief Okiti Oba-bi Olorun.
Ewang visited the area in September shortly after oil was found on the Benin side of the border and promised the 1,800 strong community better water supplies to improve their living conditions.
Nigeria has yet to commence oil exploration on its side of the border but officials said it was vital to have a strong government presence in such a potentially oil-rich area.
Virtually all of the two million barrels per day of crude oil currently produced by Nigeria is pumped from the Niger Delta area in the southeast.
